questions.stem: A cycle shop display has 9 cycles, some bicycles and some tricycles. Why can't you work out from this alone how many are bicycles?
options: Bicycles and tricycles must be counted as the same item
The problem needs a graph before any answer is possible
One equation in two unknowns has many possible solutions
The number of cycles must be split into equal halves
questions.explanation: b + t = 9 is one equation with two unknowns, so pairs such as 4 and 5 or 6 and 3 all fit. A second, independent piece of information is needed to narrow it to one pair.

questions.stem: A display has 9 cycles, each a bicycle or a tricycle; there could be none of either type. If this is all you know, how many different combinations of bicycles and tricycles are possible?
options: infinitely many
questions.explanation: The number of bicycles can be any whole number from 0 to 9, with the rest tricycles, giving 10 combinations. The context limits the possibilities to whole numbers, so there are not infinitely many.

questions.stem: A display has 9 cycles, some bicycles and some tricycles, with 23 wheels in total. How many tricycles are there?
questions.explanation: b + t = 9 and 2b + 3t = 23. Doubling the first gives 2b + 2t = 18; subtracting leaves t = 5, so there are 5 tricycles and 4 bicycles.

questions.stem: For a problem with two unknown quantities, what is needed to fix a unique solution?
options: Two linear equations that are neither equivalent nor parallel
One linear equation and a sketch of its graph on the axes
Two linear equations that have exactly the same slope
Any two equations, as long as both use the same variables
questions.explanation: Two independent pieces of information give two lines that cross at exactly one point. Lines with the same slope are either parallel, giving no solution, or the same line, giving infinitely many.

questions.stem: A plumber charges a $40 call-out fee plus $25 per hour. Which algebraic formula gives the charge y dollars for a job of x hours?
options: y = 65x
questions.explanation: The call-out fee is charged once, so it is the constant term, and $25 is added for every hour, so it is the coefficient of x. Swapping them would charge $40 per hour.

questions.stem: The plumber's charge is y = 25x + 40. On the graph of this function, what does the y-intercept of 40 represent?
options: The number of hours worked when the charge is zero
The extra amount charged for each hour of work
The total charge for a job lasting one full hour
The call-out fee charged before any work is done
questions.explanation: The y-intercept is the value of y when x = 0, which is the $40 call-out fee. The extra amount for each hour is the slope, $25.

questions.stem: In a table of values for a linear function, with x going up in steps of 1, how does the slope appear?
options: As the constant amount added to y at each step
As the value of y in the first row of the table
As the constant amount y is multiplied by each step
As the largest value of y that appears in the table
questions.explanation: A linear relationship grows by successive addition of a constant, and that constant increment is the slope. Multiplying by a constant each step describes exponential growth, not linear.

questions.stem: A numerical sequence has values 7, 11, 15, 19 for x = 1, 2, 3, 4. Which formula represents it?
options: y = x + 4
questions.explanation: The values go up by 4 each step, so the slope is 4. Stepping back from x = 1 to x = 0 gives 7 − 4 = 3, the constant term. Using 7 as the constant forgets that the first value is at x = 1.

questions.stem: A linear graph of a gym's charge (y dollars) against the number of classes (x) passes through (0, 60) and (5, 185). Which formula matches it?
questions.explanation: The slope is (185 − 60)/(5 − 0) = 25 and the graph crosses the y-axis at 60. Dividing 185 by 5 ignores the starting value of 60.

questions.stem: For the plumber's charge y dollars for a job of x hours, which statement about the variables is correct?
options: y is the independent variable and x is dependent
x and y are both independent of each other
x is dependent because hours depend on cost
x is the independent variable and y is dependent
questions.explanation: The charge depends on the number of hours worked, so hours is the independent variable and the charge is the dependent variable. The independent variable goes on the horizontal axis.

questions.stem: To enter 3x + 2y = 18 into a graphing calculator in the form y = ..., it is rearranged to:
questions.explanation: Subtract 3x from both sides to get 2y = 18 − 3x, then divide every term by 2: y = 9 − 1.5x. Dividing only the 3x by 2 leaves 18 undivided.

questions.stem: Rearranged into the form y = ..., the equation 4x − 5y = 20 becomes:
questions.explanation: Subtract 4x: −5y = 20 − 4x. Divide every term by −5: y = −4 + 0.8x. Forgetting that dividing by −5 changes both signs gives y = −0.8x + 4.

questions.stem: When pairs of simultaneous linear equations are solved by graphing on a calculator, how is the solution found?
options: By locating the point where the two lines intersect
By locating where each line crosses the vertical axis
By locating where each line crosses the horizontal axis
By comparing the slopes of the two lines that are drawn
questions.explanation: The intersection is the only point that lies on both lines, so its coordinates satisfy both equations. The axis intercepts belong to one equation each and do not solve the pair.

questions.stem: A student solves a pair of simultaneous equations by reading the intersection from a hand-drawn graph. What is the main limitation of this method?
options: The graph can only show lines with a positive slope
A graph cannot show two lines on the same set of axes
The method only works when both lines pass through zero
The coordinates may only be read approximately
questions.explanation: If the intersection does not fall on a grid point, its coordinates can only be estimated. An equation solver or algebra gives the exact values.

questions.stem: Two lines are given by y = 3x − 4 and y = 8 − x. At what point do they intersect?
questions.explanation: Setting 3x − 4 = 8 − x gives 4x = 12, so x = 3 and y = 8 − 3 = 5. The point (2, 6) satisfies the second equation only.

questions.stem: Solve the pair 2x + y = 11 and x − y = 1.
questions.explanation: Adding the equations eliminates y: 3x = 12, so x = 4, and then y = 4 − 1 = 3. Checking in 2x + y = 11 confirms 11.

questions.stem: For the pair 3x + 2y = 22 and 3x − y = 7, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Subtracting the second equation from the first eliminates x: 3y = 15, so y = 5. Then 3x = 7 + 5 = 12, so x = 4. The value 5 is y, not x.

questions.stem: Which pair (x, y) satisfies both 3x + 2y = 16 and x − y = 2?
questions.explanation: (4, 2) gives 12 + 4 = 16 and 4 − 2 = 2, so it satisfies both. (2, 5) and (6, −1) satisfy only the first equation, and (5, 3) satisfies only the second.

questions.stem: A family buys 10 cinema tickets. Adult tickets cost $15 and child tickets $8, and the total is $122. How many child tickets were bought?
questions.explanation: a + c = 10 and 15a + 8c = 122. Substituting a = 10 − c gives 150 − 7c = 122, so c = 4 and a = 6. The value 6 is the number of adult tickets.

questions.stem: A jar holds 30 coins, all $5 tokens or $2 tokens, worth $102 in total. How many $5 tokens are there?
questions.explanation: f + t = 30 and 5f + 2t = 102. Replacing t with 30 − f gives 3f + 60 = 102, so f = 14 and t = 16. Fifteen of each would be worth $105.

questions.stem: A concert sold 600 tickets: A-reserve at $45 and general admission at $30. Ticket revenue was $21 600. How many general admission tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: a + g = 600 and 45a + 30g = 21600. With g = 600 − a: 15a + 18000 = 21600, so a = 240 and g = 360. The value 240 is the A-reserve count.

questions.stem: Electrician Spark charges $90 plus $60 per hour; electrician Volt charges $50 plus $70 per hour. For how many hours do they charge the same amount?
questions.explanation: Setting 90 + 60h = 50 + 70h gives 40 = 10h, so h = 4. Both then charge $330.

questions.stem: Spark charges $90 plus $60 per hour and Volt charges $50 plus $70 per hour. For a 6-hour job, which is cheaper, and by how much?
options: Volt, by $20
Spark, by $40
Volt, by $40
Spark, by $20
questions.explanation: Spark charges 90 + 60 × 6 = $450 and Volt charges 50 + 70 × 6 = $470. Beyond the 4-hour break-even point Spark's lower hourly rate makes it cheaper; Volt's $40 saving on the call-out fee only wins for shorter jobs.

questions.stem: At a market, 3 kg of apples and 2 kg of bananas cost $17.30, while 1 kg of apples and 4 kg of bananas cost $13.10. What is the price of apples per kilogram?
questions.explanation: 3a + 2b = 17.30 and a + 4b = 13.10. Substituting a = 13.10 − 4b gives 39.30 − 10b = 17.30, so b = 2.20 and a = 4.30. $2.20 is the price of bananas.

questions.stem: Tank A holds 800 L and loses 25 L per hour. Tank B holds 200 L and gains 35 L per hour. How much water is in each tank when they hold the same amount?
questions.explanation: 800 − 25t = 200 + 35t gives 60t = 600, so t = 10 hours. Then each tank holds 800 − 25 × 10 = 550 L. 500 L is just the average of the starting volumes.

questions.stem: A pair of equations is x + 2y = 8 and 2x + 4y = 16. How many solutions does the pair have?
options: Exactly two, one for each of the equations
Infinitely many, because they are the same line
None, because the two lines are parallel
Exactly one, where the two lines intersect
questions.explanation: The second equation is the first multiplied by 2, so both describe the same line and every point on it is a solution. Parallel lines would need the same slope but a different intercept.

questions.stem: A pair of equations is x + 2y = 8 and x + 2y = 11. How many solutions does the pair have?
options: None, because the two lines are parallel
Infinitely many, because they are the same line
Exactly one, where the two lines intersect
Exactly one, at the point where y = 0
questions.explanation: The left sides are identical but cannot equal both 8 and 11, so no pair (x, y) works. Graphically the lines have the same slope and different intercepts, so they never meet.

questions.stem: Two linear equations in a problem turn out to be equivalent. What does this say about the information given?
options: It gives exactly one solution to the problem
It gives exactly two solutions to the problem
It is insufficient to fix a single solution
It is inconsistent, so there is no solution
questions.explanation: Equivalent equations carry the same information, so they describe one line and leave infinitely many possibilities. Inconsistent information is the case where the lines are parallel.

questions.stem: At a cafe, 2 coffees and 3 muffins cost $23.50, and 4 coffees and 6 muffins cost $47.00. What can be concluded about the prices?
options: They cannot exist, because the two orders give inconsistent information
A coffee costs $4.25 and a muffin costs $5.00, the only possible pair
A coffee costs $3.50 and a muffin costs $5.50, the only possible pair
They cannot be found, because the second order gives no new information
questions.explanation: The second order is exactly double the first, so 4c + 6m = 47 is equivalent to 2c + 3m = 23.50. Pairs such as $4.25 and $5.00 work, but so do many others, so the prices are not fixed.

questions.stem: At a cafe, 2 coffees and 3 muffins cost $23.50, and on the same day 4 coffees and 6 muffins cost $45.00 at the same prices. What can be concluded?
options: The information is inconsistent, so no prices fit both orders
The information is insufficient, so many prices fit both orders
A coffee costs $1.25 less than a muffin, the only possible pair
The second order shows that muffins cost $2.50 less each
questions.explanation: Doubling the first order gives 4c + 6m = 47.00, which contradicts 45.00. The equations represent parallel lines, so no pair of prices satisfies both, and the data must contain an error.

questions.stem: Which pair of equations has infinitely many solutions?
options: 2x − y = 4 and 6x − 3y = 4
2x − y = 4 and 2x + y = 4
2x − y = 4 and 4x − y = 8
2x − y = 4 and 6x − 3y = 12
questions.explanation: 6x − 3y = 12 is 3 times 2x − y = 4, so the equations are equivalent. 6x − 3y = 4 is parallel with no solution, and the other two pairs cross at the single point (2, 0).

questions.stem: A bus company says a trip for 3 adults and 2 children costs $26, and a trip for 6 adults and 4 children costs $52. What extra information would fix the adult and child fares?
options: The cost of a trip for 12 adults and 8 children
The cost of a trip for 2 adults and 1 child
The cost of a trip for 9 adults and 6 children
The cost of a trip for 6 adults and 4 children
questions.explanation: The two given trips are equivalent, since the second is double the first. A trip for 2 adults and 1 child is not a multiple of 3 adults and 2 children, so it adds an independent equation. The other trips are multiples of the first.

questions.stem: A trip for 3 adults and 2 children costs $26, and a trip for 2 adults and 1 child costs $15. What is the adult fare?
questions.explanation: 3a + 2c = 26 and 2a + c = 15. Doubling the second gives 4a + 2c = 30; subtracting the first leaves a = 4, and then c = 15 − 8 = 7.

questions.stem: A student solves a contextual problem by listing possibilities for each condition and finding a pair that appears in both lists. What is this method, and what is its drawback?
options: Trial and error; it can never find a whole-number answer
Trial and error; it is slow when there are many possibilities
Graphing; it only gives an estimate of the intersection point
Equation solving; it needs every equation in the form y = ...
questions.explanation: Listing numerical possibilities and matching them is trial and error. It works for small problems but becomes inefficient as numbers grow, which is why graphing or an equation solver is used.

questions.stem: In a contextual problem, what does the solution of a pair of simultaneous equations give?
options: A list of every pair that meets at least one condition
Values of both unknowns that meet every condition at once
Values of one unknown that meet the first condition only
The slope and intercept of each line in the problem
questions.explanation: A solution must satisfy both equations, so it is the one pair of values that meets all the stated conditions together. A pair meeting only one condition lies on only one of the lines.

questions.stem: How does inconsistent information in a pair of linear equations appear when the equations are graphed?
options: As two lines meeting on the vertical axis
As two lines meeting at right angles
As two parallel lines that never meet
As one line drawn on top of the other
questions.explanation: Inconsistent equations have the same slope but different intercepts, so their lines are parallel and there is no point on both. One line on top of the other shows equivalent equations, where the information is insufficient.

questions.stem: Why are equations such as 5x + 2y = 30 usually rearranged before being entered into a graphing calculator?
options: Rearranging changes the solution to a whole number
The calculator needs the slope to be a positive value
Graphing mode needs each line in the form y = ...
The calculator can only graph equations with no y
questions.explanation: Most graphing tools plot functions entered as y in terms of x, so 5x + 2y = 30 becomes y = 15 − 2.5x. Rearranging does not change the solution, only the form of the equation.
